questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to check your blind spot if you use your mirrors.
Your mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can trust that other drivers will see your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: How should you check your tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire to see if it looks full.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare your tire to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check your tire pressure before every ride. A tire that looks okay may actually be under-inflated, so you cannot rely on your eyes alone.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs tell you the rules you must follow on the road.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots too small to be a problem.
Have blind spots that you need to check by turning your head.
Have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you need to check by turning your head.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT help reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injuries, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose clothing made of tough materials for the best protection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, which is true?

options.text: You can go faster than the speed limit while passing.
You can ignore "No passing" markings if you started in a passing zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must complete the pass at the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass at the speed limit and in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must complete your pass at or below the speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Like cars, motorcycles have blind spots. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Only look in your mirrors.
Use your side vision.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before changing lanes.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see clearly to the sides.
Limits how far you can see.
Is usually uncomfortable.
Has no markings or labels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see clearly to the sides for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels and markings showing the manufacturer's name and safety standards.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes but not your face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Do not work as well as eyeglasses.
Provide no protection at all.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses are not enough protection for either your eyes or face.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not use your headlight.
Use your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Always use your headlight.
Use your headlight only if you want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Always use your headlight when riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers much more likely to see you.

questions.question: You have had alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still remain.
You will be okay as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body can process about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your body. Your abilities and judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: Which material offers the best protection for motorcyclists?

options.text: Leather
Wool
Polyester
Silk

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely when riding.

questions.question: Before you ride, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and holds the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You are stopping other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. This way, the driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more than side mirrors.

questions.question: For the best protection, a helmet should:

options.text: Have a few cracks.
Not be certified.
Have frayed straps.
Fit snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Check your tires for all of the following, except:

options.text: Air pressure.
Tread.
General wear.
Flexibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, general wear, and tread.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Use only the front brake.
Reduce your speed.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have small blind spots that should not concern you.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular part of your scanning.

questions.question: To lower your risk of a crash:

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Wear dark clothes.
Ride in parts of the lane where you are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and scan the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes smoothly and gradually for the shortest and safest stops. Do not let either tire skid.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should the operator do?

options.text: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
Go faster.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not warn passengers about dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. The operator must stay farther back from the vehicle ahead to stay safe.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, what should you do with them?

options.text: Tuck them in.
Leave them loose.
Remove them from your shoes.
Glue them together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tuck them in.
questions.explanation: Tuck your shoelaces in securely while riding. Loose laces can catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing where to position your motorcycle in a lane?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which part of the lane makes your trip shorter.
Whether you can pass more vehicles in one position than another.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should allow other drivers to see you and give you enough space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: If you think it will take longer than usual to stop your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay farther back from the vehicle ahead.
Stay closer to the vehicle ahead.
Leave the road.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: If stopping will take longer, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. This is especially important on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.
